title: Hook fault (e.g. unwritable ~/.symphony) silently disables all guarding; documented faulted state never produced
why_it_matters: If the state directory can't be created or written (permission error, read-only $HOME, full disk, NFS hiccup), StateStore.update raises inside store.py's _locked()/_write() and propagates to main()'s bare except, which writes one stderr line and returns exit code 0. Exit 0 tells the host the hook succeeded, so every subsequent tool call, subagent spawn, and Stop proceeds completely unguarded -- no SYMPHONY_ROLE gate, no completion gating, no assessment requirement -- with zero host-visible signal. The project's own docs (skills/symphony/references/provider-activation.md) define a `faulted` activation state for exactly this ('a hook command or packaged file failed'), but no production code path ever writes that state; it only appears in scripts/package_smoke.py's own simulated result list. The fix should make main() distinguish 'hook raised' from 'hook denied a tool' and persist a faulted marker (or at minimum emit an inject_context/stderr message a human is likely to see) instead of a bare stderr line plus exit 0.

why_it_matters: On Codex, when an assessor/consultant/lead subagent stops without satisfying Symphony's contract (low-effort assessor, unclassified consultant decision, wrong-tier lead), runtime.py's _observe_delegation produces an inject_context action carrying the corrective instruction (e.g. "The assessor result was not produced at high effort or above.
